who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), plain-store lane round 5, blaze-merge-1113
where: crates/blaze-keyed/src/kind.rs Kind; crates/blaze-cas/src/plain/handle.rs PlainStore's impl of blaze_keyed::store::Store
what: Store's read, map and put take a Key<K: Kind>, and Kind needs a Layout, Grain, Trace, Keep and a Root: Headed, with no impl anywhere in the tree to borrow, so the plain store's Store impl (lock-free reads, own proofs for uncommitted puts, Uncommitted from map) got no test: a test kind would mean guessing all of these without a compiler.
cost: the trait impl lands untested; its behaviour is tested only through Plain and Driven underneath it
cause: the trait is written against the full record-kind machinery, and nothing gives a store test a minimal kind
class: an interface whose only argument types are expensive to make, so every implementer's test needs the whole stack
prevention: blaze-keyed ships a #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-kinds"))] kind (bytes in, bytes out) that every Store implementer's tests use
workaround: none; the impl is reviewed against Plain's tested reads and puts
